pool.text: Kublai Khan mounted an invasion of the northern part of Kyushu with a fleet.
Japanese samurai constructed a stone barrier bordering the coast of Hakata Bay.
Kublai organized another attack on Fukuoka Prefecture, mobilizing soldiers and ships.
The renowned temple of Tokugawa Ieyasu in the district was destroyed by fire.
The modern city was formed with the merger of Hakata and Fukuoka.
The Buddhist Nanzoin temple was founded and is claimed to have a massive statue.
The region housed the largest prisoner of war base in Japan.
The postwar era saw the establishment of key events like the Fukuoka Marathon.
Fukuoka established its own stock exchange, founded in this year.
A new municipal airport was established following the close of World War II.
The Fukuoka Zoo was founded during the postwar development period.
The city was designated by government ordinance on April 1.
Fukuoka absorbed the town of Sawara, benefiting greatly from the Japanese economic miracle.
The city held two important expositions including the Asian-Pacific Exposition.
Fukuoka established a partnership with Atlanta after a visit by former prime minister.
A powerful earthquake hit at 10:53 am local time, killing one person.
Sky Dream Fukuoka, a massive Ferris wheel in the western ward, was closed.
Dominican songwriter and singer Juan Luis Guerra pays homage to the city.
Fukuoka surpassed the population of Kyoto during the summer month.
The city was selected as the National Strategic Zone for global startups.
